entries.originalText: It behoveth thee to learn to mortify thyself in many things, if thou wilt live in amity and concord with other men.
entries.modernizedText: You must learn to mortify yourself in many things if you want to live in friendship and harmony with others.

entries.originalText: It is no small thing to dwell in a religious community or congregation, and to live there without complaint, and therein to remain faithful even unto death.
entries.modernizedText: It is no small thing to dwell in a religious community or congregation, to live there without complaint, and to remain faithful there even unto death.

entries.originalText: Blessed is he who hath lived a good life in such a body, and brought it to a happy end.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed is the person who has lived a good life in such a body and brought it to a happy end.

entries.originalText: If thou wilt stand fast and wilt profit as thou oughtest, hold thyself as an exile and a pilgrim upon the earth.
entries.modernizedText: If you want to stand firm and benefit as you ought, consider yourself an exile and a pilgrim on the earth.

entries.originalText: Thou wilt have to be counted as a fool for Christ, if thou wilt lead a religious life.
entries.modernizedText: You will have to be counted a fool for Christ if you want to lead a religious life.

entries.originalText: The clothing and outward appearance are of small account; it is change of character and entire mortification of the affections which make a truly religious man.
entries.modernizedText: Clothing and outward appearance are of small account; it is change of character and complete mortification of the affections that make a truly religious person.

entries.originalText: He who seeketh aught save God and the health of his soul, shall find only tribulation and sorrow.
entries.modernizedText: Whoever seeks anything except God and the health of his soul will find only tribulation and sorrow.

entries.originalText: Nor can he stand long in peace, who striveth not to be least of all and servant of all.
entries.modernizedText: Nor can anyone stand long in peace who does not strive to be least of all and servant of all.

entries.originalText: Thou art called to endure and to labour, not to a life of ease and trifling talk.
entries.modernizedText: You are called to endure and to labor, not to a life of ease and trifling talk.

entries.originalText: Here therefore are men tried as gold in the furnace.
entries.modernizedText: Here, therefore, people are tested like gold in the furnace.

entries.originalText: No man can stand, unless with all his heart he will humble himself for God’s sake.
entries.modernizedText: No one can stand unless he humbles himself with all his heart for God’s sake.
